messages.subject: Re: tutorial on ggplot2
parts:
Dear all,

please could you recommend an organized, easy to follow, logical tutorial  on ggplot2, that would explain ALL the arguments in a ggplot2 function with the SPECIFIC SETTINGS of each argument ? many thanks,

bogdan

On Tue, Dec 22, 2015 at 6:49 AM, <ggp...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
ggp...@googlegroups.com Google Groups
Topic digest
View all topics
  • looping figure creation, but needing to input different species name each iteration - 1 Update
looping figure creation, but needing to input different species name each iteration
henn...@d.umn.edu: Dec 21 09:27AM -0800

Hi Dennis,
 
I'll be aware of your suggestions next time. Thanks.
 
Your suggestions worked quite well. The key to modifying what I had done
to get it all to work was the addition of nesting atop inside of bquote.
 
myplot<- subset(anon, species==i)
my_title<-bquote(atop(paste("Mean Suitability for ", italic(.(i)), " by
Year"), "Anonymous National Park"))
 
thanks so much for you help. This will be a huge time saver.
 
Kris

messages.subject: Re: tutorial on ggplot2
parts:
I should also mention that Hadley just released ggplot2 version 2.0.0 and one of the major things he did was update the documentation so that it does not have so many … references. It does not look like the package documentation updates made it over to docs.ggplot2.org yet, so I would also suggest just using the package documentation as well, e.g.,

update.packages("ggplot2”) # make sure you have version 2.0.0
library(ggplot2) 
?geom_line # or whatever you are curious about

messages.author: 12a8430c1bf3f70b
messages.subject: Re: tutorial on ggplot2
parts:
Bogdan,
I'd second Wayne's recommendation of Winstons book.  I had used ggplot since the early draft of Hadley's book - which I read on holidays! :)  However, it was only when I needed to do lots of different plots that I found myself reaching for Winston's book every five minutes... so when you ask yourself "how do I do X in ggplot2?"... you reach for Winston's excellent book and the odds are it will have the answer.  There are still a few slightly more obscure things that aren't in there... but if you're at that point, you come to this list! :)

All that said, I've already pre-ordered the second edition of Hadley's book! :)

cheers and good luck!
Sean

Your suggestions worked quite well. The key to modifying what I had done
to get it all to work was the addition of nesting atop inside of bquote.
 
myplot<- subset(anon, species==i)
my_title<-bquote(atop(paste("Mean Suitability for ", italic(.(i)), " by
Year"), "Anonymous National Park"))
 
thanks so much for you help. This will be a huge time saver.
